subject: docs/implementation/m3/resume-repair-jrw/PROPOSAL.md

requiredFindings.problem: A zero schema cookie does not exclude every committed-history state reachable through the SQL/VACUUM writers the law includes. The law acknowledges wraparound but calls it unreachable, while still claiming that cookie 0 establishes that no schema change or evidence ever committed. SQLite implements a wrapping 32-bit counter; defensive mode does not turn it into an unbounded history counter.
evidence: The pinned product selects rusqlite =0.40.2 with bundled SQLite (crates/storage/Cargo.toml:13), and enables defensive mode at crates/storage/src/ledger_store.rs:125-133. Its controls impose no lifetime schema-change bound.
The libsqlite3-sys 0.38.2 primary documentation identifies the bundled engine as SQLite 3.53.2: https://docs.rs/crate/libsqlite3-sys/0.38.2 .

SQLite 3.53.2 src/build.c:1934-1958 explicitly acknowledges that repeated schema changes can return the cookie to a previous value and increments it using unsigned arithmetic: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sqlite/sqlite/version-3.53.2/src/build.c .

SQLite 3.53.2 src/vacuum.c:329-352 uses u32 meta, adds 1 to BTREE_SCHEMA_VERSION, and preserves text encoding, user_version and application_id: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sqlite/sqlite/version-3.53.2/src/vacuum.c .

Static counterexample, not executed: start at cookie 0 in a private WAL database; commit CREATE TABLE t(x), INSERT, and DROP TABLE, then complete 2^32-2 ordinary VACUUM operations. The committed schema increments total 2^32, so the cookie returns to 0. The schema is empty and VACUUM permits the same one-page, zero-freelist footprint with UTF-8 and zero IDs. No raw-byte write, writable_schema, schema_version assignment, or non-defensive operation is required.
RW-C5's finite fixtures reject the original compacted-history example but do not establish the claimed universal history guarantee or make wraparound unreachable.
requiredFindings.fix: Make the no-wrap premise explicit and qualify every history guarantee by it. State that the relevant file history begins at cookie 0, has fewer than 2^32 committed schema-cookie increments, and has no reset/forgery; say this is a custody/producer-history assumption, not a fact L-UNC can infer. Remove the claim that wrapping is unreachable through ordinary SQLite interfaces and qualify the coverage of arbitrary SQL/VACUUM writers accordingly. Carry the same premise into the basis, RW-S3 and X-RW-9. If the law retains its universal guarantee instead, it needs an independent history discriminator or must keep C-LEDGER withdrawn for histories it cannot establish. Keep the positive-view stop rule and N-L0 fallback; a wraparound stress run is not requested.

requiredFindings.problem: N-T2 assigns installation-incomplete to every symlink or non-directory at a publication parent name, and RW-C15 requires that result. At the pinned baseline these cases fail the native directory open and take HOST.IO_FAILURE, before the custody judgment that produces installation-incomplete. Implementing the stated result would change an existing public refusal row, contrary to the law's unchanged-row rule.
evidence: At e093e90, crates/security/src/trust/floor_publication.rs:434 calls open_private before any directory creation/completion; :164-166 maps a child-directory open failure through lift(TrustRow::HostIo), whereas :170 maps a failed private-directory judgment through lift(TrustRow::Incomplete).

crates/platform/src/filesystem/directory_open.rs:61-73 turns only NotFound into None and retains every other native failure. :134-150 opens with O_DIRECTORY and O_NOFOLLOW and returns the native error for a non-directory or symlink.
floor_publication.rs:58-69 preserves the supplied row for an operation failure and uses the budget row separately.

At e093e90, crates/security/src/trust/current_trust_admission.rs:84-110 maps HostIo to HOST.IO_FAILURE with no installation-incomplete subject; Incomplete maps to CONFIG.CUSTODY_REFUSED with that subject.

Accepted X4T r11 item 10, docs/implementation/m2/trust-admission-x4t/PROPOSAL-r11.md:153, preserves host I/O and budget rows. RW-N12's particular non-empty ACL-omitted directory does reach the custody judgment, so its installation-incomplete expectation is correct.
requiredFindings.fix: Split N-T2 by the existing failure boundary: a directory opened successfully whose custody/predicate fails keeps CONFIG.CUSTODY_REFUSED / installation-incomplete; native child-directory open failures, including symlink/non-directory failures, keep HOST.IO_FAILURE; budget failures keep their budget row. Apply that distinction to item 3.6 and RW-C15. Authorize C-ACL only after obtaining the retained directory and observing precisely P-ACL; do not recover a native I/O failure by reclassifying it. Keep RW-N12 unchanged.

nonBlockingObservations.problem: The census state coverage is adequate, but the prose conflates distinct point identities with physical trace records. Host traces -a and -b do not have the same create.after bases, and the storage trace includes the directory point in both commit and refused-end children.
evidence: The storage trace contains 1379 records and 22 create.after bases. dependency/create.after#6 occurs at line 112 in commit and line 1256 in refused-end.

Host trace -a contains 1009 records and 11 create.after bases; -b contains 165 records and 7 bases. Their union has 14 bases; their respective journal witness paths differ. Both contain the predecessor-directory point at line 40 (#5).
The separately manifest-verified host trace -c contains 21 records and no create.after point.

Thus there are three referenced trace/point selections (storage #6, host -a #5, host -b #5), but four physical directory events across the recorded publishing children. Neither storage #6 nor host #5 is in its target kill set.

The extra storage event leaves the same RW-T3 state. RW-D1 already selects the commit driver explicitly; the differing host bases remain covered by the P states or the existing journal owners. No additional L11 state or mandatory new RW row was found.
nonBlockingObservations.fix: Describe host -a and -b as sharing the dependency shape, list their different base sets or refer to the union, and distinguish the three trace/point selections from the four physical directory events. Explicitly note storage's refused-end occurrence. Preserve the existing RW-D1/RW-K10 state coverage.

requestItemAssessments.detail: Defensive mode and cookie 0 reject the r1 compacted-history fixture. RW-C5 requires both positive bundled-engine views and negative fixtures before enabling completion. Failure withdraws completion without widening the predicate and preserves L11/N-L0. Those gates are sound as law, but their future execution is not evidence of a no-wrap history bound.

Cases (a)/(b) exactly impose absent N plus absent marker, or complete N plus an absent/equal/prefix marker. Present marker with absent N is excluded before every effect. N-R9's ACL-omitted and private-malformed rows match project_admission.rs:602-603,616,684-685. No IE passage successor is required.

requestItemAssessments.detail: C-TDIR is after the unchanged reference-directed fenced read and under the publication fence. It is limited to may_create names and empty, same-filesystem, owner/private-mode ACL-omitted directories. It finishes both directory barriers before publication continues. RW-D1 adds the unsampled directory explicitly; RW-K10 covers its repair barriers; RW-N12 is a correctly labelled mutation; no-ExecutionId cells are skipped; future reference transcriptions, existing driver use and evidence-gated L11 retirement follow X9 r16.
The three original observations are addressed without changing the intended byte-preservation or equal/prefix rules.
